claims.text: Optimizing laser-based additive-manufacturing parameters will reduce fabrication-induced defects relative to conventional parameters.
Optimizing laser-based additive-manufacturing parameters will improve dimensional precision relative to conventional parameters.
Optimizing laser-based additive-manufacturing parameters will improve the mechanical integrity of high-entropy-alloy components relative to conventional parameters.
High-entropy-alloy components produced using standard laser-based additive manufacturing have fabrication-induced defects and dimensional variability.
The intervention consists of modifying laser power, scan speed, layer thickness, and hatch spacing during fabrication.
Adjusted process parameters will enhance melt-pool dynamics and produce more uniform solidification.
Adjusted process parameters will reduce thermal gradients and residual stress.
Reduced thermal gradients and residual stress will decrease defect formation and improve dimensional accuracy.
Optimized process parameters modulate energy input and cooling rates.
Modulating energy input and cooling rates reduces localized overheating and uneven solidification.
Reduced localized overheating and uneven solidification minimize porosity and residual stress.
Lower porosity and residual stress produce denser material and improved phase consistency.
Denser material and improved phase consistency lead to better dimensional and mechanical properties.
Specimens produced with optimized parameters will exhibit lower deviation from design tolerances than conventionally produced specimens.
Specimens produced with optimized parameters will exhibit increased yield strength and ultimate tensile strength relative to conventionally produced specimens.
The expected improvement is limited to the tested high-entropy-alloy compositions, geometries, and laboratory-scale additive-manufacturing systems.
Powder quality and beam focus may affect the intervention's results.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements at p < 0.05 in both dimensional precision and mechanical strength will falsify the hypothesis.
